subject: Clinical Scoring Systems
title: Emergency & Trauma Scores: GCS, Wells & Parkland
preview: Recognize the Glasgow Coma Scale, the clinical probability role of the Wells score, and why modern burn fluid resuscitation is titrated.

sections.title: Neurologic assessment with GCS
points: Record eye, verbal and motor components separately and repeat assessments over time.
A low GCS prompts urgent airway assessment but does not replace evaluation of airway reflexes, oxygenation and other causes of reduced consciousness.

sections.title: Pulmonary embolism risk before testing
points: Use Wells or another validated rule in the intended population, incorporating clinical context, D-dimer and imaging when appropriate.
Probability estimates are less reliable when used outside their validated setting.

sections.title: Burns: titrate rather than blindly follow a formula
points: For adults with large burns, the American Burn Association recommends a lower initial fluid estimate than the historical Parkland 4 mL/kg/%TBSA approach, to reduce fluid-related harm.
Repeated urine-output and perfusion assessments guide adjustments in a specialized care pathway.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: Record each component rather than only a summed total.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Do not treat a historical burn-fluid formula as an unchangeable prescription.
Neither a low GCS nor a positive probability score replaces professional clinical assessment.

quickRevision: GCS assesses eye opening, verbal response and motor response; individual components and the clinical context matter.
Wells criteria estimate pretest probability of pulmonary embolism and help direct appropriate testing.
Burn fluid formulas are starting estimates; resuscitation should respond to patient physiology and specialist guidance.

quiz.question: What does the Glasgow Coma Scale evaluate?
quiz.explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale records eye, verbal and motor responses; each component can change independently and should be documented.

valueSources.label: Adult major-burn initial fluid estimate
valueSources.source: American Burn Association Clinical Practice Guidelines on Burn Shock Resuscitation (Journal of Burn Care & Research, 2024)
valueSources.note: For adults with ≥20% TBSA burns, an initial 2 mL/kg/%TBSA estimate is recommended; titrate to response.
